incidents.cause: The pilot’s decision to continue the visual flight rules flight into an area of instrument meteorological conditions, which resulted in the pilot’s spatial disorientation and a loss of control of the helicopter. Contributing to the accident was the inadequate oversight of the flight by Omniflight’s
The failure of the starflex arm during engine run-up due to inadequate inspection by maintenance personnel.
The pilot's excessive taxi speed, which resulted in a loss of control and subsequent nose over.
The pilot’s decision to land on unsuitable terrain, which resulted in a loss of control and a collision with trees.
The pilot's failure to maintain adequate airspeed during landing in variable gusting crosswind conditions, which resulted in a hard landing and runway excursion.
The manufacturing defects in the main landing gear leg, which resulted in its eventual failure.
The pilot’s misjudged landing flare, which resulted in a hard landing.
An in-flight collision with a bird resulting in damage to a tail rotor blade, which required replacement.
The pilot’s failure to maintain clearance from power lines during low level aerial application operations due to a distraction.
The pilot’s failure to maintain directional control during the takeoff roll.
The pilot’s failure to maintain directional control during the landing roll with a tailwind.
The pilot’s decision to depart in turbulent and gusting wind conditions, which resulted in a loss of control and impact with terrain.

The pilot’s improper landing flare, which resulted in a hard landing on upsloping terrain, and his subsequent failure to maintain adequate airspeed and his exceedance of the airplane’s critical angle of attack during an attempted go-around, which resulted in an aerodynamic stall.
An encounter with convectively induced turbulence during descent.

The local control controller’s poor judgment in duty prioritization which distracted them from monitoring arriving and departing traffic and resulted in a runway incursion and loss of same runway separation. Contributing was the operations supervisor’s decision to troubleshoot a faulty flight strip
